title: Energy and Speed Are Related
bigQuestion: How are energy and speed related?
sourceRanges: Teacher Guide Lesson 4 Investigating Energy and Speed, printed p. 33
Teacher Guide Lesson 5 Energy and Speed Are Related, printed p. 39
concepts: Speed is a measurement of the distance an object travels over an amount of time.
Compare the same object at different speeds.
Objects pick up more speed on steeper ramps (Reader p. 15).
Greater speed of that object is related to greater energy of motion.
The evidence is a greater observed change.
Students are not required to quantitatively measure speed or energy.
Ramp It Up 2.0 measures ramp height and target movement in centimeters.
Cup movement is evidence of the greater change, not a speed measurement.
exclusions: ramp height is a measurement of speed

anchors.title: Big Question
lines: How are energy and speed related?
anchors.speakerNote: Ask the question. Do not give the relationship yet.

anchors.title: Vocabulary — Speed
lines: speed — a measurement of the ____ an object travels over an amount of time.
blankPositions: the word after measurement of the
anchors.speakerNote: On the write slide, do not say the missing word. Reveal it only on the reveal slide.

anchors.title: One Ball, Two Speeds
lines: Compare the ____ ball at two speeds.
A bigger ____ is how we know the faster ball had more energy of motion.
anchors.speakerNote: Teach this before any measured Ramp It Up trial. Do not say the missing words on the write slide.

anchors.title: Ramp and Target Preview
lines: Roll one ball from a lower setup and from a higher setup. Say which cup move was bigger. Do not measure. Do not say a speed number.
anchors.speakerNote: One ball. Two setups. Students name the bigger cup move. No centimeters and no speed number.

anchors.title: Ramp It Up 2.0
anchors.protocolStatement: Ramp It Up 2.0 uses one ball. Heights come from 1, 2, and 3 books. Measure the vertical ramp height in centimeters. Measure how far the target moves in centimeters. Run one calibration trial and do not record it. Record three trials at each height. That is nine measured trials. Graph ramp height in centimeters against average target movement in centimeters. Do not write a speed in meters per second. Ramp height is not a measurement of speed. The engineering challenge is to move the target as close as possible to 30 centimeters without going past.
anchors.speakerNote: Do not record the calibration trial. Nine measured trials. No speed number. Ramp height is not speed.

anchors.title: What We Measured
lines: We measure how far the ____ moves in centimeters.
We do not measure a speed number.
The one thing we change is ramp ____.
anchors.speakerNote: Ramp height and cup movement are measured in centimeters. Speed is not measured. Cite TG Lesson 4 Ramp It Up (AP 4.1), not Reader pp. 13-14.

anchors.title: Ramp Height and Average Movement
lines: The graph axes are ramp height in centimeters and average target movement in centimeters.
anchors.speakerNote: Do not label either axis as speed. Do not write meters per second.

anchors.title: Steeper Ramp
lines: Objects pick up more ____ on steeper ramps.
From the steeper ramp, that ball made a ____ change.
blankPositions: what increases on a steeper ramp
anchors.speakerNote: Reader page 15. Teach the source fact first: objects pick up more speed on steeper ramps. Then the observation: the same ball made a greater change. Cup movement is evidence of the greater change, not a speed measurement.

anchors.title: The Bounce
lines: The faster ball bounced ____ than the slower ball.
anchors.speakerNote: Reader page 16. A louder sound is also a bigger change. Do not say the missing word on the write slide.

anchors.title: Your Thinking
lines: How are energy and speed related? Name the ball you kept and one change that was bigger.
anchors.sampleAnswer: That ball had more energy of motion when it caused a greater change. I did not measure a speed number.
anchors.speakerNote: Open writing. Accept the same object, a greater change, and no speed number.

anchors.title: Big Question Now
lines: How are energy and speed related?
anchors.sampleAnswer: For the same object, greater speed is related to greater energy of motion. A greater change is the evidence.
anchors.speakerNote: Students answer after CHECK. This is not the Monday first-thinking slide.

anchors.title: Drop It
lines: Optional Friday investigation. Drop the same ball from two heights into sand. Compare the craters. The required relationship was already taught.
anchors.speakerNote: FLEX only. Do not introduce the speed relationship here.

anchors.title: Friday Recovery
lines: Catch-up, review, finish notes, quiz or makeup, and optional enrichment.
anchors.speakerNote: Friday may assess or finish work already taught. It does not open a new required idea.

assessment.scope: Students explain the relationship for the same object by using a greater observed change. They are not required to calculate a speed or an energy quantity.

quiz.when: Friday 2026-10-23 or makeup within 2 school days

itemsPlan.prompt: Speed is a measurement of the ____ an object travels over an amount of time.
What is the evidence of greater energy of motion?
In Ramp It Up 2.0, what did we measure in centimeters? Name both things.
What was the one thing changed in Ramp It Up 2.0?
Which pair of axis labels is allowed?
The same ball rolls from a steeper ramp. What greater change do you look for?
How are energy and speed related?

practice.role: Apply the same-object rule to a new everyday example. Do not recopy the notes.

recovery.requiredMakeup: Finish Guided Notes BQ, V1, N1, N2, N3, N4, CHECK, and BQ_NOW. Use the Reader catch, ramp, and bounce examples. Do not invent centimeter measurements the student did not take.
recovery.labMakeup: If the lab was missed, the student explains the relationship from the Reader. The teacher may show the class graph. The student does not copy fake personal data.
recovery.dropIt: Drop It is not required makeup.
recovery.quizMakeup: If a quiz was given, makeup is within 2 school days.
